summary_en: Nichirin updated its capital efficiency targets: DOE floor of 2.5%, dividend payout ratio of 45%, and annual dividend of 190 yen per share (95 yen interim + 95 yen year-end). The company plans to acquire and cancel up to 1.5 billion yen of treasury shares to enhance per-share value. Over 2026–2028, the company allocated 35 billion yen to capital: 20.5 billion yen for strategic investments, 13 billion yen for shareholder returns, and 1.5 billion yen for other purposes.
title_en: Financial Results for the Six-Month Period Ending June 2026 and Progress on Initiatives toward Management Conscious of Capital Cost and Stock Price
translation_en_brief:
Nichirin disclosed updated capital efficiency targets and shareholder return plans as part of its management philosophy centered on capital cost and stock price awareness. The company set a dividend payout ratio target of 45% and a DOE (Dividend on Equity) floor of 2.5%, supporting an annual dividend forecast of 190 yen per share comprising 95 yen interim and 95 yen year-end dividends.

The company intends to acquire up to 1.5 billion yen of treasury shares through market purchases, with the acquired shares to be cancelled. This initiative aims to improve capital efficiency and enhance per-share value for shareholders. As of the interim settlement date, the company had progressed 55 billion yen or 15.9% of its 2026–2028 capital allocation framework.

Over the 2026–2028 period, Nichirin allocated a total of 35 billion yen across capital deployment: 20.5 billion yen for strategic investments, 13 billion yen for shareholder returns (inclusive of the treasury share repurchase), and 1.5 billion yen for other purposes. The company maintained its full-year operating profit guidance at 9.3 billion yen, revising only the foreign exchange assumption for the second half from 150 yen to 160 yen per US dollar to account for currency headwinds and operational uncertainties including the 2024 Kumamoto earthquake impact.
